question.leadin: Answer the following about the office of Vice President.
question.text: This man became the first person to succeed from Vice President to President following the death of William Henry Harrison.
question.clue: That Secretary of State under this President negotiated a treaty that settled the border between Maine and Canada called the Webster-Ashburton Treaty.

swap.leadin: Name some people who reached the West Coast after much tribulation.
swap.text: This group that was accompanied by Shoshone guide Sacagawea endured freezing cold and numerous diseases before sighting the Pacific. Surprisingly, only Charles Floyd perished on this exploratory mission.
swap.answerHtml: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark Expedition [accept Corps of Discovery Expedition; prompt on partial answers]
swap.answer: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark Expedition
swap.clue: This group gifted their winter residence, a wooden fort on the Columbia, to Coboway, chief of the Clatsop natives.

question.leadin: The Wilmot Proviso attempted to outlaw slavery in any territories gained during this conflict.
question.text: Name this war between neighboring countries that ended in 1848 with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
question.clue: As a representative, Abraham Lincoln doubted the validity of this war via the Spot Resolutions, and a philosopher refused to support either slavery or this war by paying his poll tax, as noted in Civil Disobedience.

swap.leadin: Rufus King was the last presidential candidate of this party, and he lost in a landslide in 1816.
swap.text: Name this early American political party, which counted John Adams and Alexander Hamilton among its members. The failure of the Hartford Convention led to the demise of this party.
swap.clue: The Coodies were a faction of this party from Maryland.

question.text: During the American occupation of Florida, this general garnered controversy by executing Alexander Arbuthnot and Robert Ambrister for aiding Seminole resistance fighters.
question.clue: He killed the Nicholas Biddle-led Second Bank of the U.S. with the Specie Circular and signed the Indian Removal Act.

swap.text: The Committee of Detail based their draft of the Constitution on state constitutions, the Articles of Confederation, and this politician's Virginia Plan. This man wrote, "If men were angels, no government would be necessary" in Federalist No. 51.
swap.clue: This man argued that the president's powers are strictly bound by the Constitution as "Helvedius" in the Helvidius-Pacificus debates.

question.text: This man who was President of the Mormon Church at the time of the massacre banned priesthood of African-American males in the church. He also resisted the US Army in the Utah War, or "Buchanan's Blunder."
question.clue: He founded a Cooperative Mercantile Institution to maintain economic control after his "Sebastopol policy" failed to forestall the installation of Alfred Cumming as governor by the army of A. S. Johnston.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about early industry in the United States.
swap.text: Starting in the 1820s, this Massachusetts city northwest of Boston used Southern cotton and a workforce of locally-hired girls to produce textiles in its mills.
swap.clue: The Rhode Island system was succeeded by a system named for Waltham and this city, which hired young people between 15 and 35 to work in centralized, strictly supervised factories.

question.leadin: Name these conferences of early American history.
question.text: This meeting, attended by five states, was held at the same time as negotiations for the Treaty of Ghent. Several constitutional amendments were proposed, but it was a proposal of secession that caused the death of the Federalist party.
question.clue: Further regulations endorsed by this meeting would have prohibited consecutive presidents from being from the same state and limited the office of president to one term.

swap.leadin: Name these leaders of slave revolts.
swap.text: This freeman was hanged in 1822 for allegedly plotting a revolt in Charleston, South Carolina.
swap.clue: He gained notoriety after becoming a "class leader" in the AME church and preaching that his followers were the "New Israelites," though he already had a successful carpentry business purchased with proceeds from a $1500 lottery prize.

question.leadin: Name these early Supreme Court cases.
question.text: The executor of the estate of Robert Farquhar attempted to sue the state of Georgia in this 1793 case, which led to the adoption of the Eleventh Amendment.
question.clue: This first significant Supreme Court case, which ruled that the federal court had the power to hear cases in which private citizens sued states.

swap.leadin: This party's few electoral victories included Chicago mayor Levi Boone, whose ordinances provoked the Lager Beer Riot.
swap.text: Name this nativist political party that briefly gained popularity in the 1850s. This party's common name arose from the oaths of secrecy taken by its predecessor, the Order of the Star Spangled Banner.
swap.answerHtml: Know Nothing Party [or American Party or Native American Party]
swap.clue: Its members often quoted the speeches of Lewis Levin, who was elected to Congress in Pennsylvania in the wake of riots in Philadelphia.

question.leadin: In response to these documents, their target slandered his opponent by accusing him of pimping out a young American girl to the Tsar of Russia.
question.text: Name these pamphlets that contained vicious personal attacks accusing one candidate of consuming the corpses of defeated Native Americans while slandering his wife over the charge of alleged bigamy during the 1828 election.
question.clue: This documents released by Philadelphia news editor John Binns during the election of 1828.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Monroe administration.
swap.text: The Panic of 1819 caused many to question the integrity of this body headed by Nicholas Biddle. Its constitutionality had been established in the 1819 case McCulloch v. Maryland.
swap.answer: Second Bank of the United States
swap.clue: An opponent of this organization was the first cabinet appointee to be rejected by the Senate, after his recess appointment expired.

question.leadin: Answer some things about money in the United States.
question.text: In order to prevent state governors from having authority to forgive debts, Hamilton pushed for this clause to be included in the Constitution. It also prohibits states from making treaties and was used as the basis of Fletcher vs. Peck.
question.clue: The Supreme Court rejected the petitioners' argument that the creation of the Warren Bridge was in violation of this clause of the Constitution. This clause was also the basis for the decision in Fletcher v. Peck.

swap.leadin: This party was the first one that future Republican Thaddeus Stevens was involved in.
swap.text: Name this third party that nominated William Wirt for the presidency in 1832. It was one of the first parties to use nominating conventions and party platforms in American history.
swap.clue: The disappearance and possible murder of William Morgan in upstate New York fueled the creation of this party.

question.text: In the 1790s, this African-American polymath created an early American almanac and included his dialogues with Thomas Jefferson on slavery. This man is also attributed with creating the first American-made clock.
question.clue: This African American architect and astronomer reconstructed Pierre L'Enfant's layout for Washington D.C. from memory.

swap.leadin: This event saw soldiers onboard the steamboat Warrior murder more than 150 Indians over two days, ignoring a white flag waved on the first day.
swap.text: Identify this event that occurred in the aftermath of the Battle of Wisconsin Heights, and involved a militia firing under the command of General Henry Atkinson.

question.leadin: Answer the following about expeditions to find the source of the Mississippi River.
question.text: In 1805, Louisiana Territory governor James Wilkinson ordered this brigadier general to find the source of the river. The Spanish captured him in Colorado, the state that contains a peak named for him.
question.clue: He died leading the amphibious assault on the British garrison at York during the War of 1812.

swap.leadin: Name these men involved in the history of the telegraph, FTP each.
swap.text: In 1845 this man became Morse's business manager and helped promote rapid expansion of the telegraph service. He had earlier served as Postmaster General under Andrew Jackson and Martin Van Buren.
swap.clue: He donated his home and property, known as his namesake "green," to serve as Gallaudet University for deaf children.
